noetic-sample-g8-01.title: Use the middle day
noetic-sample-g8-01.body:
The five numbers go up by 6 each day, so the middle (3rd) day is the average: $215 \div 5 = 43$.

The 1st day is two steps earlier: $43 - 2 \times 6 = 31$.

**Answer: 31 math problems**

noetic-sample-g8-01.title: Equation
noetic-sample-g8-01.body:
If he solved $x$ on day 1, the total is $x + (x+6) + (x+12) + (x+18) + (x+24) = 5x + 60$.

$5x + 60 = 215 \Rightarrow x = 31$.

**Answer: 31 math problems**

noetic-sample-g8-02.title: Try each number of large boxes
noetic-sample-g8-02.body:
Solve $9L + 4S = 30$:

- $L = 0$: $30 \div 4$ isn't whole.
- $L = 1$: $21 \div 4$ isn't whole.
- $L = 2$: $12 \div 4 = 3$ ✓
- $L = 3$: $3 \div 4$ isn't whole.

So 2 large and 3 small boxes: $2 \times 15 + 3 \times 9 = 30 + 27 = 57$ dollars.

**Answer: \$57**

noetic-sample-g8-02.title: Use parity
noetic-sample-g8-02.body:
$4S$ is even and 30 is even, so $9L$ must be even: $L$ is 0 or 2 (since $9L \le 30$). $L = 0$ needs $4S = 30$, impossible. So $L = 2$, $S = 3$.

Cost: $\$30 + \$27 = \$57$.

**Answer: \$57**

noetic-sample-g8-03.title: Height is the side of the square
noetic-sample-g8-03.body:
The square's area is $10 \times 10 = 100$ in², so the triangle's area is 30 in².

Take $EF$ as the base. P is on AB, so the height from P to line CD is the side of the square, 10 in.

$\frac{1}{2} \cdot EF \cdot 10 = 30 \Rightarrow EF = 6$ in.

**Answer: 6 inches**

noetic-sample-g8-03.title: Compare with a half-square
noetic-sample-g8-03.body:
Any triangle with base $CD$ (10 in) and apex on $AB$ has area half the square, i.e. 50% of it.

With the same height, area is proportional to the base. We want 30%, which is $\frac{30}{50} = \frac{3}{5}$ of 50%, so $EF = \frac{3}{5} \times 10 = 6$ in.

**Answer: 6 inches**

noetic-sample-g8-04.title: Position of each hand
noetic-sample-g8-04.body:
Measure angles clockwise from 12.

- Minute hand at 20 minutes: $20 \times 6° = 120°$.
- Hour hand: at 2:00 it is at $60°$, and it moves $0.5°$ per minute, so at 2:20 it is at $60° + 10° = 70°$.

Angle between them: $120° - 70° = 50°$.

**Answer: 50°**

noetic-sample-g8-04.title: Count the gap
noetic-sample-g8-04.body:
At 2:20 the minute hand points exactly at the 4. The hour hand is $\frac{20}{60} = \frac13$ of the way from the 2 to the 3.

From the hour hand to the 3 is $\frac23$ of $30° = 20°$; from the 3 to the 4 is another $30°$. Total $50°$.

**Answer: 50°**

noetic-sample-g8-05.title: Use 30-60-90 triangles
noetic-sample-g8-05.body:
In an equilateral triangle the altitude $AD$ hits the midpoint of $BC$, so triangle $ADC$ has half the area: 4 in².

Triangle $ADC$ has angles $90°$ at D, $60°$ at C, $30°$ at A. Its altitude $DP$ splits it into two triangles similar to it.

- Triangle $DPC$ has hypotenuse $DC$, which is half of $AC$ (since $DC = \frac12 BC = \frac12 AC$). Similar triangles with sides in ratio $\frac12$ have area ratio $\frac14$, so area$(DPC) = \frac14 \cdot 4 = 1$.
- Area$(ADP) = 4 - 1 = 3$ in².

**Answer: 3 in²**

noetic-sample-g8-05.title: Find where P cuts AC
noetic-sample-g8-05.body:
Let $AC = 4$ (scale doesn't matter for ratios). Then $DC = 2$, and in the right triangle $DPC$ with the $60°$ angle at C, $PC = DC \cos 60° = 1$.

So $AP = 3$, i.e. $AP : AC = 3 : 4$. Triangles $ADP$ and $ADC$ share the height from D to line AC, so their areas are in ratio $3 : 4$.

Area$(ADP) = \frac34 \times 4 = 3$ in².

**Answer: 3 in²**
